stackTraceLimit
static stackTraceLimit: number;

The Error.stackTraceLimit property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by new Error().stack or Error.captureStackTrace(obj)).

The default value is 10 but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes will affect any stack trace captured after the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will not capture any frames.

Inherited from
Error.stackTraceLimit

Methods

captureStackTrace()
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;

Creates a .stack property on targetObject, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which Error.captureStackTrace() was called.

const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with ${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}.

The optional constructorOpt argument accepts a function. If given, all frames above constructorOpt, including constructorOpt, will be omitted from the generated stack trace.

The constructorOpt argument is useful for hiding implementation details of error generation from the user. For instance:

function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();

addProvider()
addProvider(provider): this;

Add a source of actions that changes while the server runs: a Surface bridge, a registry the application rebuilds as its page changes. The provider is consulted after the actions added with register() whenever actions are enumerated or looked up by name, so the manifest, /axe/state, and the derived MCP tools reflect the current set on every request. Names must still be unique across register() and every provider (spec [P-ACT-2]); a collision is an ActionDefinitionError when the set is next enumerated.

approveHandoff()
approveHandoff(handoffId, decision): Promise<HandoffDecision>;

Record that a person approved an approval request (spec §9.3, [P-APPR-3]). Call it only from the site's own approval page, in a request authenticated by the person's session and protected against cross-site forgery, after the page has decided that approver may approve this operation. The runtime checks the rest: the handoff exists, is an approval request of this tenant, has not expired, been used, cancelled, or invalidated, and the action's approvalState still equals the state bound at the request; if the state moved, the request is invalidated for good and the reason is state_changed.

cancelHandoff()
cancelHandoff(handoffId, decision?): Promise<HandoffDecision>;

Record that a person cancelled a handoff (spec §9.3, [P-APPR-5]): an approval request, open or approved, or any other handoff. A later resume is refused with conflict and details.handoffStatus: "cancelled", and nothing runs. A handoff whose resume already ran, or is running, cannot be cancelled (used): that work is committed, and undoing it is the site's own action. Call it from the site's own page, like approveHandoff.

MemoryIdempotencyStore

In-memory IdempotencyStore. Every method runs without awaiting between its read and its write, so claims are atomic among all runtimes in one process that share the instance. Nothing survives a restart and nothing is shared with another process.

Retention is bounded ([P-LIM-4]): expired entries are swept on writes at most once per sweepIntervalMs, and at maxEntries the oldest completed entries (and claims whose lease has passed) are evicted first. An evicted completed entry shortens the idempotency window for that key: a retry after eviction runs the handler again. A claim whose lease is still running is never evicted; when every entry is one, claim throws. No timer runs, so nothing keeps a process alive.

MemoryTokenStore

In-memory TokenStore with expiry. Suitable for a single process. Retention is bounded ([P-LIM-4]): expired records are swept on writes at most once per sweepIntervalMs, and at maxEntries the oldest records are evicted (an evicted token answers not_found). No timer runs, so nothing keeps a process alive.

Interfaces

ActionProvider

A source of actions that change while the server runs (spec [S-AXE-1]: one action per live control). The server consults providers, after the actions registered with register(), whenever it enumerates actions (the manifest, /axe/state, the MCP tool list) or looks one up by name (an invocation, a continue, a resume, a poll). Every action a provider returns is built with action(), so it was linted when it was built; the server checks its auth mode and its name's uniqueness when it first sees it.

The state an approval of this action is bound to (spec §9.3), for example { planId, rev }. Required for an action whose handler returns requestApproval. The runtime calls it when the request is made, when a person approves, and when the agent resumes; the approval stands only while the value is equal (compared as canonical JSON). Keep it small: the fields whose change should void the approval.

maxBodyBytes?
optional maxBodyBytes?: number;

Largest request body the runtime reads, in bytes (spec [P-LIM-1]). A larger body is refused with invalid_input, details.reason: "payload_too_large", and HTTP 413, before it is parsed: on a Content-Length above the limit nothing is read, and a body without one is read only up to the limit. Default 1048576 (1 MiB). A body parser in front of the runtime that has already consumed the body applies its own limit first (docs/deploying.md, "Limits and retention").

operationLeaseSeconds?
optional operationLeaseSeconds?: number;

How long an operation claim holds before a retry of the same operation may take it over, in seconds. Default 60. Set it above your slowest handler: a retry that arrives after the lease runs the handler again (docs/deploying.md, "Operations, claims, and crashes").

policies?
optional policies?: Policies;

requestPolicy?
optional requestPolicy?: RequestPolicyConfig;

Content-type and origin rules for POSTs, applied before any body is read (spec [P-TRANS-1] to [P-TRANS-4]). Default: JSON required on state-changing endpoints, and a POST carrying a Cookie header must come from the origin of baseUrl or a trusted origin.

requireIdempotencyKey?
optional requireIdempotencyKey?: boolean;

Reject mutating calls without idempotencyKey. Default true.

revision?
optional revision?: RevisionProvider;

Live state (spec §21). When set, every envelope carries rev, a request whose expectedRev differs from the current revision is refused with conflict before anything runs, and /axe/state is served.

secret?
optional secret?: string;

HMAC secret for tokens, at least 16 characters. Omit only in development: a random per-process secret is used and tokens do not survive restarts.

tenant?

Resolve the tenant for a request on multi-tenant platforms. Return null for unknown hosts.

requestApproval

Ask a person to approve this exact call before it runs (spec §9.3). Return it from an action's handler for a consequential operation. The agent receives needs_human with a handoff to url, the site's own approval page; the runtime records the call's input, the acting principal, the tenant, and the state the action's approvalState reports now. The person approves or cancels on that page with approveHandoff or cancelHandoff; the agent then calls /axe/resume, and onResume runs with approval set only while the approval stands and the state still matches. An agent cannot approve its own request: nothing it can send marks the handoff approved.

A completed operation: the fingerprint it ran with and the envelope it produced.

Properties

createdAt

Epoch milliseconds when the operation completed.

Hash of what makes a retry the same operation: the canonical input for an action call, the kind and payload for a continuation. A claim with another fingerprint is a conflict.

result
result: Result;

IdempotencyStore

Storage for operation claims. Keys arrive already scoped by operation type, tenant, action, and acting principal. Every method must be atomic with respect to every other caller sharing the store, across processes: a get followed by a set is not a claim. See MemoryIdempotencyStore (one process) and SqliteIdempotencyStore in @axe/core/node (a shared SQLite file, and the SQL to port to another database).

RequestPolicyConfig

createAXE({ requestPolicy }): how the runtime treats browser-shaped POSTs.

Properties

originCheck?
optional originCheck?: OriginCheck;

"cookie" (default): check Origin on a POST that carries a Cookie header. "always": check it on every POST that names an origin, cookie or not, for sites whose browsers hold other ambient credentials (HTTP authentication, client certificates). "off": never check it; the site enforces CSRF protection itself, in front of the runtime.

requireJsonContentType?
optional requireJsonContentType?: boolean;

Refuse a POST to a state-changing endpoint unless its Content-Type is application/json or application/*+json. Default true.

trustedOrigins?
optional trustedOrigins?: string[];

Origins, besides the origin of baseUrl (and of a tenant's baseUrl), whose browser requests may carry ambient credentials. Exact origins such as https://app.example: a scheme, a host, and a port when it is not the default. No wildcards, no paths. Origins listed in cors.origins with cors.allowCredentials are trusted as well.

The agent receives needs_human with a handoff to url, the site's own approval page; the runtime records the call's input, the acting principal, the tenant, and the state the action's approvalState reports now. The person approves or cancels on that page with approveHandoff or cancelHandoff; the agent then calls /axe/resume, and onResume runs with approval set only while the approval stands and the state still matches. An agent cannot approve its own request: nothing it can send marks the handoff approved.

TokenStore

Storage for token records. Implement with Redis, a KV store, or a database for multi-instance deployments. The in-memory implementation is the default. Records are written when a token is minted and when completeHandoff records a completion; single use is enforced by an operation claim in the IdempotencyStore, so this store needs no atomic operation.

type HandoffRefusal = 
  | "not_found"
  | "not_approval"
  | "already_approved"
  | "cancelled"
  | "invalidated"
  | "used"
  | "state_changed";

Why approveHandoff or cancelHandoff refused. not_found covers an unknown id, an expired handoff, and another tenant's, alike.

HandoffStatus

type HandoffStatus = "open" | "completed" | "approved" | "cancelled" | "invalidated" | "used";

Where a handoff stands, as getHandoff reports it: open (waiting for the person), completed (completeHandoff recorded it), approved (approveHandoff), cancelled (cancelHandoff), invalidated (an approval whose bound state changed), or used (a resume ran it, or is running it now).
